newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN refugee agency assists Rwanda genocide tribunal.
newsitem.headline: UN refugee agency assists Rwanda genocide tribunal.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Friday it was formally cooperating with a U.N. tribunal hunting ringleaders of Rwanda's 1994 genocide.

In the first such cooperation in Gabon, UNHCR said it was assisting investigators from the U.N. war crimes tribunal probing the Hutu-led slaughter of more than half a million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus.

Spokeswoman Pam O'Toole said two tribunal officials were interviewing 123 Rwandan refugees in Gabon. A large proportion were soldiers of the former government army, which played a key role in the genocide, and included high-ranking ex-officers.

UNHCR was also screening about 100 Rwandan Hutus in the Central African Republic to determine whether they were genuine refugees and hoped to start a similar operation for around 2,500 refugees in Angola, O'Toole told a Geneva briefing.

The U.N. tribunal, created in November, 1995, has indicted 23 genocide suspects of whom 19 are in custody at its seat in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha. Many organisers of the slaughter remain at large.

Well-known alleged ringleaders of the genocide openly lived in sprawling camps in former Zaire run by the UNHCR before they were forced to flee by Tutsi-dominated rebels who subsequently took Kinshasa.
The UNHCR had come under heavy criticism for failing to separate soldiers and Hutu rebels from the civilian refugee population at those camps on the edge of Rwanda.
